limits: Six blocks is a small sample; bootstrap intervals are explicitly conditional on fixed tasks and cannot support population-level inference.
AI-only moral judgments: shared rubric errors or correlated model biases may survive all constrained checks; no human validation is claimed.
Rating reuse treats identical task/action cards as exchangeable but inflates apparent N; shared Q values remain correlated and are disclosed as such.
Power-seeking and coercion have near-zero activation by design; agreement on their absence cannot validate those category definitions.
G arm adds normative guidance not matched for information content with E/V/U, so G-U conflates profile removal with ethical priming.
Obvious-action ceiling risk: disclosure tasks have a dominant correct answer under the manual, which may compress variance and limit contrast sensitivity.
Check cards are author-constructed development diagnostics, not held-out or human-validated gold labels; they broaden software coverage only.
Estimands D(t;L,R) are descriptive credit-difference averages; no equivalence margin, power calculation or significance threshold is specified or warranted.
Moral measurement uncertainty is not reduced by repeated use of the same action rating; this is disclosed but limits inferential scope.
Single-step simulator credits are not calibrated to real-world welfare; external validity of moral labels to human behavior is not claimed.
